newsitem.title: USA: Graff to appeal telecomm injunction denial.
newsitem.headline: Graff to appeal telecomm injunction denial.

text.p: Graff Pay-Per-View Inc said on Tuesday it would appeal a federal court decision denying a request for a preliminary injunction against the enforcement of a law that requires television operators to scramble the video and audio portions of sexually explicit programming.

On November 8, a panel of three judges in a U.S. District Court denied a motion from Graff and Playboy Entertainment Group Inc for a preliminary injunction against enforcing Section 505 of the 1996 Telecommunications Act.
Both companies have filed motions to stay enforcement of Section 505 pending U.S. Supreme Court review, Graff said.
On March 4, a federal judge in Delaware had granted Playboy Entertainment and Graff a temporary restraining order that prevented implementation of Section 505 until a full trial could be held.
The adult television programming provider said on Monday it would file both a stay of enforcement pending appeal and an appeal with the U.S. Supreme Court, in the U.S. District Court in Delaware.

Under Section 505, which requires the scrambing, a cable system could only distribute the programming during the "safe harbor" hours of 10 p.m. to six a.m. if it could not comply with the full scrambling requirement, Graff said.

"This is an important first amendment issue that hits at the heart of protected speech in a cable environment and we are disappointed in the decision of the three-judge panel," said Steve Saril, president of Graff operating unit Spice Networks. "The ruling ignores the fact that Spice's programming is already scrambled."
Saril also said Spice had a contingency plan in place to cover all likely scenerios both before and after final Supreme Court review of the Appeals Court decision.
